curriculum.lesson_evidence: A written scene plan is the evidence for this lesson, pulling the unit's skills into one original fiction. The plan names where, when, and who; the opening offer you will accept; each character's objective; one status choice shown by posture or by who decides; one spoken line and its subtext; and an entrance or exit that changes who decides. It also names the consent rule: no touching without agreement, voices at speaking level, and an adult nearby if anyone performs. Performance is optional. A blank page is not evidence, even if the scene was tried in the lounge. The plan also repairs one misconception from this unit, such as thinking status belongs to the adult, or thinking a block is clever. Write the old mistake, the corrected idea, and a one-line example that could happen inside your new scene. Do not copy a published play. Invent the fiction yourself.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A classmate's plan says only that two people will be funny in a shop. Which missing pieces must be added so this is a real improvised scene plan?

FEEDBACK
Add the opening offer, each character's objective, one circumstance, and the consent rule before anyone performs. Funny is not yet a fiction. The plan needs a fact to accept, a want for each person, a where or when or who, and a clear no-touch agreement. Status, subtext, and an entrance can follow, but those four pieces stop the plan being a blank joke. Acting the shop scene without writing them does not replace the plan.

WATCH FOR
Leaving the page blank because the scene was acted in the lounge treats the performance as the only evidence. This lesson asks for the written plan, including the repaired misconception. A performance can happen afterwards, only with a consenting partner and an adult supervising, and it is still optional. The page is what you submit.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Write a full scene plan for a new fiction, not the library or lost property, and repair one misconception. Include where, when, and who; the opening offer; each objective; one status choice shown by posture or decision; one line of dialogue with subtext; an entrance or exit that changes who decides; and the consent and safety rule. Then name one old mistake from this unit, the corrected idea, and a one-line example inside your new scene. Do not copy the jumper plan. If you perform, everyone agrees and an adult supervises. The writing is the required evidence.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
A useful plan sets the lost-property room just before home time and accepts that the jumper is not in the box. Where: lost-property room. When: five minutes before home time. Who: Sam and the office helper. Offer accepted: 'Your jumper is not in the box.' Objectives: Sam wants a next place to look; the helper wants the room locked on time. Status: the helper plays low status by asking Sam which place to try next, shown by waiting with the keys still. Line and subtext: Helper: 'The box is the only one I checked.' (Want: Sam should know the search was small.) Exit: the helper leaves with the keys, so Sam must decide the next place alone. Consent: no touching, speaking voices, adult in the room if performed. Misconception repair: high status is not the adult. In this plan the helper can play low status by letting Sam decide.

TRY FIRST
A classmate's plan says only that two people will be funny in a shop. Which missing pieces must be added so this is a real improvised scene plan?

FEEDBACK
Add the opening offer, each character's objective, one circumstance, and the consent rule before anyone performs. Funny is not yet a fiction. The plan needs a fact to accept, a want for each person, a where or when or who, and a clear no-touch agreement. Status, subtext, and an entrance can follow, but those four pieces stop the plan being a blank joke. Acting the shop scene without writing them does not replace the plan.
